sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: The Big Questions Family Almost all of us live in a family.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: The family is the fundamental and most ancient unit of any society.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: In Indian society today, there are several types of families — from joint families to nuclear families.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: A joint family has several generations living together — grandparents, parents, uncles and aunts, Love and dharma are the flower and fruit of family life. — Tiruvalluvar Examples of joint families

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: In English, there are not many terms to describe family relationships; we saw some of them in the first paragraph.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: For example, in Hindi there is bua, tau, tai, chacha, mausi, nana, nani, and many more.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Some languages, such as Tamil, also have different terms for elder brother / sister or younger brother / sister.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: But what is the word for ‘cousin’ in an Indian language?

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: In most Indian languages, you will find that there is no such word!

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: That is because cousins are only ‘brothers’ and ‘sisters’.
